statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt is now twenty-eight hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; twenty-one of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress holds at 57 in the elevated band: the Saudi East-West pipeline that normally carries 4% to 5% of global oil supply remains shut after drone strikes, Houthi forces hold Perim island and the Bab el-Mandeb exit, and pricing for a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC stands near 87% after August core CPI printed 0.3% month over month against a 0.2% estimate. Confidence is 87 in the high band: the index level, VIX, the H.15 yield curve, crude, rate-hike pricing, the seven-day calendar and the Red Sea sequence were each re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the only structurally unavailable input is live price path.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in twenty-one of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so a score that measures a pathological price path cannot be elevated across hours in which no path can form. Second, the last observed session granted mean reversion rather than denying it, and did so against a hawkish input: August CPI printed with core slightly hot at 0.3% against a 0.2% estimate and hike odds jumped to roughly 87%, yet the index still closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point range, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. Advancing issues led decliners by about 2.1 to 1 and nine of eleven sectors closed higher, so there is no shallow-pullback, failed-retracement or session-extreme evidence to carry forward. Third, the weekend escalation that supports Stress is a supply-route story rather than observed index structure, and it is partly offset by Friday's 2.37% fall in crude on news of the Hormuz talks and by the GCC-Iran meeting scheduled in Salalah on Monday. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00 UTC reopen hour and the hour that follows it, where thin liquidity can meet an unpriced weekend, rather than a broad session-wide caution. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Twenty-eight hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while the Saudi East-West pipeline carrying 4% to 5% of global oil supply stays shut and Houthi forces hold Perim island and the Bab el-Mandeb exit, leaving an unpriced supply-route weekend to meet Sunday's 22:00 UTC reopen three days before an FOMC decision priced near 87% for a hike.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. Friday's advance snapped four losing sessions but did not rescue the week: the S&P 500 closed 7,656.98 and still fell about 0.8% over the five days while the Dow lost roughly 1.6%. Breadth on the day was genuinely broad, with advancers ahead of decliners by about 2.1 to 1 and nine of eleven sectors higher. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, which is a notably calm volatility print against the macro backdrop.

That backdrop is the reason Stress sits at 57 while Tail sits at 6. August CPI, released Friday, rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year in line with estimates, but core rose 0.3% against a 0.2% estimate, and market pricing for a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC moved to roughly 87% from about 72% the prior day. The H.15 release for 10 September shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%, a heavy long end consistent with an inflation-sensitive curve. Energy is the transmission channel: WTI settled at 100.05 and Brent at 104.61, each down more than 2% on Friday but roughly 9.7% higher on the week, after drone strikes shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and Houthi forces took Mocha, Dhubab and Perim island at the Bab el-Mandeb exit. The IEA has cut its 2026 supply outlook by a further 1.4 million barrels per day.

For the twenty-four hours this forecast covers, the dominant structural fact is that the market is shut. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so twenty-one of the twenty-four forward slots contain no possible price path and the final three cover the restart and early Asian Monday trade. Conditional Tail therefore rises gradually from 6 to 19 across the closure, pricing the weekend information stock that must clear in one auction rather than any directional view, steps to 22 in the reopen hour and eases to 21 and then 20 as two-way flow returns. Those three slots map to WATCH and define the published danger window. The nearest unresolved checkpoint is the GCC-Iran foreign ministers' meeting in Salalah on Monday, the first such gathering since the war began in late February; a constructive or hostile weekend signal ahead of it would reach a market with no venue able to price it, which is precisely the deferred-repricing risk the rising curve describes rather than an assertion that any such path has been observed.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 01:00 UTC on 12 September to 00:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5 and held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across every slot, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 59 to a 50 low around 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Hormuz-talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding to 57 by the close of the window as attention turned to the reopen and to Wednesday's FOMC. Confidence stayed in an 85 to 87 band throughout.
outlookSummary: Twenty-one of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract reopens at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, which is this horizon's twenty-second slot. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates, steps to 22 in the reopen hour and eases to 21 and then 20 as two-way flow returns. Those final three slots map to WATCH and define the danger window from 22:00 UTC to 00:00 UTC. Stress rises from 57 to a 64 peak at the restart on the unresolved supply-route picture and the approach to Wednesday's FOMC, and Confidence holds an 84 to 87 band, dipping only for the mid-horizon slots where distance rather than evidence quality is the limiting factor.
